label: prf:brings-euler-characteristic
title: Proof of the Euler-characteristic computation
html:
Bring's curve is a compact Riemann surface of genus g = 4 (Bring's surface). The classification of compact orientable surfaces gives \chi_{\mathrm{eu}} = 2 - 2g, hence \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\Sigma_4) = -6.

For the Hochschild form, the Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg theorem (HKR) identifies HH_n(\Sigma_4) \cong \bigoplus_i H^i(\Sigma_4, \Omega^{i+n}). The Hodge numbers of a genus-g curve are h^{0,0} = h^{1,1} = 1 and h^{1,0} = h^{0,1} = g, so \dim HH_0 = 2 and \dim HH_1 = \dim HH_{-1} = g, and the alternating sum is 2 - 2g. Equivalently -6 = \deg T_{\Sigma_4} = \int_{\Sigma_4} c_1(T_{\Sigma_4}), the degree-two component of the Chern character of the tangent bundle (Chern character). \square
